item.title: Napoleonic triangles on the sphere from similar chord triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.21408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a variant of Napoleon's construction on the unit sphere, in which the triangles erected on the sides of a spherical triangle $ABC$ are required to have similar isosceles chord triangles with apex angle $\beta\in(0,\pi/2)$. For a non-equilateral $ABC$, we prove that the triangle $XYZ$ of spherical circumcentres is equilateral if and only if $\cos(\theta_a+\theta_b+\theta_c\pm\Omega/2)=0$, where $\theta_a,\theta_b,\theta_c$ are the base angles of the isosceles spherical triangles $XBC$, $YCA$, $ZAB$, $\Omega$ is the area of $ABC$, and the sign $+$ (resp.~$-$) corresponds to the outward (resp.~inward) construction. We derive from this an explicit classification in terms of two quadrics and a cubic inequality. It recovers the theorem of Dipierro, Noakes and Valdinoci for $\beta=\pi/3$, and exhibits three families of solutions for $\beta>\pi/3$, together with a fourth one when $\cos\beta<1/4$.
item.dc:creator: Quang Hung Tran

item.title: On the Solution Sets of the Cone-Volume Map
item.description: arXiv:2610.21533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed set $U=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ of outer unit normals, we consider the cone-volume map which associates to a vector of support numbers $b\in\mathbb R^m_{> 0}$ the cone-volume vector $\gamma\in\mathbb R^m$ of the polytope \[ P(U,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:U^\top x\leq b\}. \] We study its fibers $S(U,\gamma)$ over prescribed cone-volume vectors $\gamma$, with particular emphasis on finiteness and non-uniqueness. We give characterizations of the irreducibility of $U$ in terms of properties of the cone-volume map and its solution sets. In particular, for irreducible $U$, we show that $S(U,\gamma)$ is finite for all $\gamma$ outside a set of measure zero in the cone-volume cone, and we give an explicit upper bound for its cardinality. In the planar case, we prove that $S(U,\gamma)$ has semialgebraic dimension at most one for arbitrary $U$. Moreover, for every $U\in\mathcal{U}(2,m)$ with $m\geq 4$, there exists a cone-volume vector $\gamma$ for which $S(U,\gamma)$ contains at least two distinct elements. As a consequence, there exist two distinct smooth planar convex bodies with the same cone-volume measure. Finally, for $U$ in general position, we show that the number of solutions is odd for every cone-volume vector outside the exceptional set.
item.dc:creator: Tom Baumbach, Zhang Chen, Martin Henk

item.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.
item.dc:creator: Chunna Zeng, Xiaoyu Cheng

item.title: The Rate of the Delsarte Bound for Binary Codes and Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.21263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the asymptotic rate of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes. This extends previous work of the author which formulated and proved an analogue of the conjecture of Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini for binary codes, obtaining the rate of the Delsarte linear program at distance $1/2-1/\pi$. The lower bounds introduce ideas from potential theory into the study of Delsarte's bounds, whereby the measures underlying a system of orthogonal polynomials give an obstacle problem. We solve the resulting obstacle problem in the case of binary codes and spherical codes, obtaining a closed form for the lower bound in terms of elliptic integrals. For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Salmon

item.title: Lattice coverings by parallelotopes containing cube vertices
item.description: arXiv:2610.21572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate when a parallelotope containing vertices of the unit cube $Q_n=[0,1]^n$ covers $\Bbb R^n$ by integer translates. We prove the covering property for every parallelepiped containing five vertices of $Q_3$, and, in any dimension, for every parallelotope containing a facet of $Q_n$ and one vertex of the opposite facet. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp bound $1/n$ for the volume of a pyramid contained in $Q_n$ with a parallelotope base. We also give an alternative proof of this bound.
item.dc:creator: Dragomir Grozev, Nikolai Nikolov

item.title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} \pi(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $\pi$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.
item.dc:creator: Eeva Kuure, Markus Myllyoja, Aleksi Py\"or\"al\"a

item.title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.21775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Braun, Nicola Gigli, Robert McCann, Simone Vincini

item.title: The rank problem for metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a complete, second countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank. This answers a well-known question posed by Fokina, Friedman, K{\"o}rwien and Nies, and shows that the known upper bound $\omega_1$ on the rank, proved by Doucha, is sharp. Further, a Baire category based variant of the rank of metric spaces is developed, and this is used to give new proofs of the known rank bounds based only on standard methods of descriptive set theory.
item.dc:creator: Asger Tornquist

item.title: Metric geometry for ranking-based voting: Tools for learning electoral structure
item.description: arXiv:2602.10293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop the metric geometry of ranking statistics, proving that the two major permutation distances in the statistics literature -- Kendall tau and Spearman footrule -- extend naturally to incomplete rankings with both coordinate embeddings and graph realizations. This gives us a unifying framework that allows us to connect popular topics in computational social choice: metric preferences (and metric distortion), polarization, and proportionality. As an important application, the metric structure enables efficient identification of blocs of voters and slates of their preferred candidates. Since the definitions work for partial ballots, we can execute the methods not only on synthetic elections, but on a suite of real-world elections. This gives us robust clustering methods that often produce an identical grouping of voters -- even though one family of methods is based on a Condorcet-consistent ranking rule while the other is not.
item.dc:creator: Moon Duchin, Kristopher Tapp

item.title: Local stability for the truncated octahedral conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.03093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note proves that the truncated octahedron of Archimedes is a strict local minimizer of the isoperimetric quotient among parallelohedra in three dimensions. This extends the corresponding result from the five-dimensional lattice-Voronoi subclass to the full ten-dimensional local parameter space. A six-zone parametrization and Schur's lemma reduce the Hessian to two positive definite $2\times 2$ matrices.
item.dc:creator: Lark Song

item.title: Non-convex polytopes realizing kissing contact graphs in dimensions 5-7
item.description: arXiv:2609.12640v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Each of the 12 known conjecturally optimal kissing configurations in dimensions 5, 6, and 7 carries a contact-graph polytope: a polytope whose vertices are the configuration points and whose edges are exactly its contacts. Eight of these polytopes are non-convex and distinct from their convex hulls, which include longer edges. Each polytope is radial about the sphere's center: its boundary meets every ray from the center exactly once. It is the unique radial polytope with those vertices and edges. Seven of the nine non-lattice configurations carry polytopes constructed from the lattice contact polytope in the same dimension by splitting some facets and reassembling the pieces. This split-and-reassemble construction describes the configurations by facets rather than by layers. The fold angles of the reassembled facets explain the inner products $1/(10-n)$, giving $1/5$, $1/4$, and $1/3$ in dimensions 5, 6, and 7, respectively. The contact graphs of all 12 configurations are infinitesimally rigid. We also prove that $Q_5$ and $R_5$ are infinitesimally jammed, extending the 10 previously established cases to all 12 configurations. All mathematical computations use exact arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Self

item.title: Mixing and Merging Metric Spaces using Directed Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.06405v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X_1,d_1),\dots,(X_N,d_N)$ be metric spaces with $d_i:X_i\times X_i\to[0,1]$ and let $X=\prod_{i=1}^N X_i$. Let $G$ be a directed graph with vertex set $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ and edge set $E(G)$. Given edge weights $P=\{p_{ij}\in(0,1]:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$, define the closed in-neighborhood $B_j(G):=\{j\}\cup\{i:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$ and put $p_{jj}=1$. Define, for $g,h\in X$, \[ d_{X,G,P}(g,h)\;:=\;1-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N\ \prod_{i\in B_j(G)}\bigl(1-d_i(g_i,h_i)\bigr)^{1/p_{ij}}. \] We prove that $d_{X,G,P}$ is a metric and analyze its behavior under graph operations (disjoint unions, Cartesian products). Two quantitative principles govern this family: (i) \emph{edge densification} (adding edges) increases the distance pointwise and in expectation, with an exact single-edge increment formula and a uniform $1/N$ sensitivity bound; and (ii) \emph{weight monotonicity}: increasing an edge weight $p_{ij}$ decreases the metric. When the coordinate pairs are independent across coordinates, we obtain a closed-form factorization of the mean distance.} In the discrete specialization $X=\mathbb{F}_q^N$ with $d_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $G$ acyclic, after replacing $G$ by the oriented reflexive transitive closure $G^{\preceq}$ of Corollary~1.4, the unnormalized distance $D_{X,G^{\preceq},P}:=N d_{X,G^{\preceq},P}$ coincides with the size of the hereditary closure of the support, yielding a poset/digraph \emph{sphere-packing bound} via the counting of lower ideals. Finally, we give a continuous analog of the construction, yielding a metric on $C([0,1],\mathbb C)$ through an explicit integral formula. These results unify and generalize several graph-based metrics used in coding theory while providing new design levers for mean-distance control.
item.dc:creator: Mahir Bilen Can, Shantanu Chakrabartty

item.title: Fiberwise amenability of \'{e}tale groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2608.09796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new amenability property for \'{e}tale groupoids, termed \textit{fiberwise amenability}, along with a stronger variant termed \emph{ubiquitous fiberwise amenability}. (Ubiquitous) fiberwise amenability emerges naturally from a coarse-geometric perspective on \'{e}tale groupoids and, in the special case of transformation groupoids, it coincides precisely with the amenability of the acting group (rather than topological amenability of the action). It is also tightly linked to the existence of invariant measures on the unit space of the groupoid. The coarse-geometric framework for \'{e}tale groupoids that we develop systematically in this work allows us to establish several foundational properties of (ubiquitous) fiberwise amenability. As an application, we prove a F\o lner--paradoxical dichotomy for minimal \'{e}tale groupoids, which will serve as a key tool in a sequel on almost elementariness of \'{e}tale groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Xin Ma, Jianchao Wu

item.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20385v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional Gaussian discrepancy, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, the so-called width of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pigati
